item.title: J.J. Watt officially announced as CBS Sports' lead NFL game analyst, replacing Tony Romo
item.description: J.J. Watt was promoted to CBS' top broadcasting crew after Tony Romo was placed on leave.
item.content:encoded:
CBS Sports made it official Thursday: J.J. Watt is the network's new lead NFL game analyst. The network confirmed Watt will continue to call games alongside Jim Nantz and Tracy Wolfson, including next season's Super Bowl.

The promotion also comes with a new multi-year deal for Watt. CBS Sports did not unveil the financial details of that agreement.

In a statement, Watt said he was "honored and grateful" for the opportunity.

"I am incredibly honored and grateful to have the opportunity to represent CBS Sports and all of the fantastic people who make this place so special," said Watt. "From the brotherhood of THE NFL TODAY to my crews calling games, I couldn't ask for better teammates alongside me on this television journey. I am thankful to David Berson for his leadership, vision and trust. I love this job and can't wait to see ya Sunday with Jim and Tracy and many more Sundays to come!"

Watt's promotion comes just a few weeks after CBS Sports split ways with former lead NFL analyst Tony Romo, who was arrested in July for suspicion of operating while intoxicated.

Following that arrest, Romo was quickly placed on leave by the network. With Romo's status still in limbo as the NFL season approached, CBS decided Watt would work alongside Nantz and Wolfson on the network's top broadcasting team. CBS' dismissal of Romo in early October further solidified Watt's position as the network's top play-by-play man.

After turning in a Hall of Fame-worthy career, Watt retired after the 2022 NFL season and joined the broadcasting world. He's risen in the field quickly, getting the top job at CBS after just a few seasons on the job.

As a broadcaster, Watt is known for his intense preparation, a trait that made him a phenomenal pass rusher back in his playing days.

item.title: JJ Watt permanently replaces Tony Romo as top game analyst for NFL on CBS
item.description: JJ Watt, the former Houston Texans defensive lineman, has been named the 'NFL on CBS' lead game analyst permanently, including for Super Bowl 62.
item.content:encoded:
The first seat in the upcoming game of NFL broadcaster musical chairs has been filled – by someone who was already occupying a coveted seat on an interim basis.

JJ Watt, the former Houston Texans defensive lineman, has been named the NFL on CBS' lead game analyst permanently, including for Super Bowl 62 in Atlanta in 2028. Watt has called games in the network's top booth with Jim Nantz (play-by-play) and Tracy Wolfson (sideline reporter) this season after the arrest and eventual departure of Tony Romo, who had held the title of No. 1 game analyst at CBS since 2017.

“I am incredibly honored and grateful to have the opportunity to represent CBS Sports and all of the fantastic people who make this place so special,” Watt said in a release announcing the news.

David Berson, chairman of the newly formed Skydance's Global Sports Group (after the merger with Paramount, CBS' former parent company), said "we are thrilled to have him leading our NFL coverage."

“I’ve had a front-row seat to JJ’s growth as a top-tier broadcaster, watching him tackle this role just like he did his Hall-of-Fame playing career,” said Berson. “He’s insightful, entertaining, passionate, meticulous in his preparation, and the ultimate teammate. He has a unique ability to see things and communicate to fans of all levels."

Watt started calling games in 2025 alongside Ian Eagle after two seasons working for CBS' long-running studio show, "The NFL Today."

“From the brotherhood of 'The NFL Today' to my crews calling games, I couldn’t ask for better teammates alongside me on this television journey," Watt said in the release. "I am thankful to David Berson for his leadership, vision and trust. I love this job and can’t wait to see ya Sunday with Jim and Tracy and many more Sundays to come!”

Watt signed a new deal that will keep him with the company.

In a video message posted on social media, Watt said he woke up Monday morning to a missed call from Berson, who told him the news. (At first, Watt joked, he wondered whether he'd been reprimanded for hurting Nantz during a booth demonstration about punching the football to force a fumble.)

“It’s an incredible honor, and it’s humbling,” Watt said. “There’s only five seats that get to do this (call the Super Bowl) … I do not take that responsibility lightly at all.

“I have an absolute blast doing it every single week and I cannot wait to continue to do it.”

From the first meeting in Arizona with David Berson & Ross Molloy, to the brotherhood of the NFL Today desk, an unforgettable year with Ian, Evan, Ken & crew and now alongside legendary Jim Nantz, Tracy Wolfson, Rikhoff and the whole crew.

What an honor & privilege.

Grateful

item.title: Giants Mailbag: How long is J.J. McCarthy's leash?
item.description: We opened up the mailbag to take your questions, comments and concerns on the latest developments in Giants land. Let’s get right to it...
item.content:encoded:
The softer spot is out of the bye, if we’re being honest. As good as J.J. McCarthy looked in the fourth quarter against the Saints (argue the situation of it later), letting Jameis Winston start against a difficult Texans team, then turning to McCarthy, made a bit more sense. He’d have two full weeks to prepare as the starter before taking on the freefalling Eagles.

But, in his brief tenure as Giants head coach, John Harbaugh has shown he doesn’t care much for what other people think. He’s going to do what he believes is best for the Giants. And, right now, he believes that is McCarthy.

So, on Wednesday, Harbaugh named McCarthy the team’s starter.

We opened up the mailbag to take your questions, comments and concerns on the latest developments in Giants land. There’s a lot on McCarthy, obviously, but some on the running back market, too.

Let’s get right to it...

How long of a leash does J.J. McCarthy have? - @ManOfSteel390

They’re going to stick with McCarthy for the foreseeable future. This is the player they targeted and wanted as their quarterback the minute Jaxson Dart went down. Now that they believe he’s ready to go, they’re going to let him see this through.

Now, playing hypotheticals, say McCarthy goes out there and looks completely and totally incapable. The Giants won’t go down with the ship simply because they sent Minnesota a fifth-round pick for McCarthy. Harbaugh has shown, in his brief time with the Giants, he’s not too proud to pull the plug on things that aren’t working.

But this is not something where a few bad throws or quarters, game or two, will lead to Winston running back out there.

What would the Giants have to see from McCarthy to give him a legit shot to compete for the starting QB job in 2027? - @DannyK731

This is among my favorite topics because of how heated people get over the hypothetical world where Dart loses his job. He is the starting quarterback for New York. The Giants plan for him to be their starting quarterback the next decade-plus. They love the player. They love the person more. Top to bottom they believe in him.

Dart is a major reason Harbaugh took this job.

Winning what is shaping up to be a dreadful division does not change that. Winning a single playoff game (ala Daniel Jones in 2022) does not change that. McCarthy would need to go on a truly remarkable run over these next 12 weeks/11 games to shake that up.

Example: Play like a top-10 quarterback in the NFL during that stretch. Lead the Giants to double-digit victories. Secure the NFC East. Then, in my opinion, get the Giants to (at least) the NFC Championship, or at the minimum, not be the reason they lose in the divisional round.

I understand how much fans believe in and love Dart, but if McCarthy can do all that, you’re probably willing to move forward with what’s working, no?

The likelihood of any of that happening is slim. In the Giants perfect world, McCarthy stabilizes the offense and helps them reach the postseason. His performance impresses enough where other teams around the league believe he can be their franchise quarterback, and compensate New York for him in the offseason.

Do you expect a similar offense with McCarthy as the Giants planned to run with Dart? - @OlympicHughes

Yes. It’s why this was never really about what Winston did or didn’t do for the Giants. The clock started the moment they traded for McCarthy. He’d be inserted into the lineup the moment a door opened, once he was mentally ready.

People are fixating too much on the word “mobility” or “running ability” with McCarthy. It’s about what he can do to help the Giants' rushing attack. He’s not a runner like Dart, or Josh Allen or Lamar Jackson, but he’s athletic enough where his legs are a part of his game.

Read options were irrelevant with Winston. The defense never expected or respected him running it. They have to with McCarthy. Winston would spin around and recklessly dazzle sometimes in the pocket, but once surrounded, it was a sack losing five, six or seven yards. With McCarthy, the hope is he can get back to the line, or pick up a few, keeping the Giants ahead of the sticks.

The Giants had to scrap so much of what they set out to do in West Virginia when Dart went down. Now, they can get back to that initial playbook. It’s what they want their identity to be.

Will Cam Skattebo get out of the dog house any time soon? - @CommishRandy

The Giants told you what they think of Skattebo in the offseason. They made a serious run at Kenneth Walker in free agency, with a willingness to hit $12 million annually to bring him aboard. They wanted Jeremiyah Lovebad in the draft. They knew he wasn’t getting past Mike LaFleur and the Cardinals.

Skattebo is a nice complement to a bellcow. The player you bring in for a physical change-of-pace. He is not a No. 1 back. He should not be getting 20-plus carries again. He’s not quick, has little burst, lacks elite athleticism, and runs into contact.

The Giants will likely try to add to the running back room before the trade deadline. It’s just a matter of if they can do anything – I have my doubts. Skattebo should leave that house, but once out of it, I’m not sure the Giants hand him the role he was enjoying pre-benching.

Where do you draw the line at acquiring a running back? Is there a money limit? - @ZooYorkSports

Not money, no. Backs are paid what they’re paid. You’ve seen Jahmyr Gibbs ($22.5 million) and Bijan Robinson ($22.25 million) reset the market. It will likely be a minute before those figures are jumped. No one with a contract set to expire is as good or better than those two. So any new contract will likely fall below that.

Even with those deals … backs are still paid so far below some of the more premium positions. Jaxon Smith-Njigba and Ja’Marr Chase are getting $42.15 million and $40.25 million per year. Cornerbacks are in the low $30Ms while Will Anderson, whom the Giants will see on Sunday, is getting a whopping $50 million per year.

The hurdle the Giants must overcome is what it will cost to get the back – team compensation. The lone expendable player the Giants have with real value is Kayvon Thibodeaux, but it’s hard to see New York dealing him (unless the wheels fall off these next three weeks) with Brian Burns on injured reserve.

The Giants have their first three picks in the next two drafts. It’s going to cost (at least) a Day 2 pick for someone like Jonathan Taylor. Personally, I’m not sure that’s worth it.

This year’s quarterback class doesn’t look as robust as it did before the season, but there will still be four, five, or six guys selected in the first round – including two or three within the first six selections. Teams with quarterbacks love to see a run on quarterbacks because it pushes elite players at other positions down.

While Harbaugh is frustrated with his current backs and the state of the run game, the smarter move is likely waiting until the offseason.

item.title: Patriots host former Chargers starter on a visit amid O-line concerns
item.description: Jamaree Salyer has 43 career stars on his NFL résumé.
item.content:encoded:
The New England Patriots offensive line has taken its hits this season, and on Thursday against the Chicago Bears will reach deep into the depths of its roster to pull out Walter Rouse and Matt Pryor as the starting guard duo. Even with them having shown some promise last week versus the Jets, depth at the position is an issue.

The Patriots consequently remain diligent, and as part of that process took a close look at a veteran guard: Jamaree Salyer, who spent the first four years of his career with the Los Angeles Chargers, was in town on Tuesday to visit with the Patriots.

Salyer, 26, originally entered the NFL in 2022 out of the University of Georgia. A one-time teammate of current Patriots center Jared Wilson, he was selected in the sixth round of the draft by the Chargers, for whom he played 67 combined regular season and playoff games with 43 starts. He joined the Dolphins this offseason but was placed on injured reserve and subsequently released in August.

While primarily serving as a backup the last two seasons, the 6-foot-4, 325-pounder does bring considerable experience and versatility to the table. The Patriots showing interest is therefore no surprise.

New England lost starting right guard Mike Onwenu to an ankle injury in Week 2, followed by his replacement Greg Van Roten going down the next week. Third-string guard Ben Brown suffered a knee injury on Sunday against the Jets, while left-side starter Alijah Vera-Tucker also exited that contest due to a hamstring injury. Onwenu and Van Roten are currently on injured reserve, while Brown and Vera-Tucker have been declared inactive for Thursday’s game in Chicago.

The Patriots’ Week 7 contest against the Bears will kick off at 8:15 p.m. ET on Thursday night.

item.title: Saints Draft Position: Entering Week 7
item.description: Two great defensive options in the first round.
item.content:encoded:
Last week, the New Orleans Saints’ draft position didn’t change after losing to the Vikings, but a win over the Giants had a major impact. Entering Week 7, the Saints are now projected to select pick 12 overall in the 2027 NFL Draft.

Georgia LB Chris Cole

Last year’s NFL Draft had an incredible linebacker duo out of Ohio State, and so far this season, Sonny Styles has been an incredible addition to the Washington Commanders, and the same is true for Arvell Reese with the New York Giants. Linebacker has become even more important in today’s NFL World, and after Demario Davis left in free agency and Kaden Elliss went down with injury, it’s clear the Saints need upgrades. Pete Werner hasn’t been bad, and Danny Stutsman is still developing, but adding a long-term, high-potential, talented LB to this group could improve everything.

Out of Georgia, Chris Cole is having a season of his own. At 6-foot-3, Cole is incredibly fast, a hard hitter, a consistent tackler, can rush the QB at OLB, is good in pass coverage, and will not stop moving. He’s one of those players that you say throughout the game, “oh, there he is again”.

Clemson CB Ashton Hampton

Sticking with defense, cornerback is still one of the Saints’ biggest needs. The Saints may have benched Kool-Aid McKinstry, but they say he had a migraine early in the game, which is why Martin Emerson Jr. was playing. It’s a bit of a confusing situation, but no matter what, the Saints need a new CB1. To find that cheap, selecting one in the first round is the way to do it, and Ashton Hampton could be that player.

For Clemson this season, Hampton has been lockdown. He is leading the nation in pass deflections and shut down one of the most talented WRs in college football, Malachi Toney. He, of course, has some things to work on, but with his length, Hampton is a lockdown corner that the Saints should consider adding to their defense.

item.title: Lions mailbag: How will Detroit defend Packers’ deep-ball attack?
item.description: Debating the best ways the Detroit Lions defense can stop the Green Bay Packers’ passing attack.
item.content:encoded:
While they may not be as effective as they seem, the Green Bay Packers do love throwing the deep ball, no pun intended. Quarterback Jordan Love has attempted more passing attempts of 20+ air yards than any other quarterback, and this is nothing new. Green Bay has ranked in the top-five of attempted deep shots in every season but one, dating back to at least 2018 (they were eighth in 2025).

Unfortunately for the Detroit Lions, they have been terrible at defending deep passes. This season, the Lions rank 32nd in EPA/pass (+1.41), 31st in yards per game (80.6), and 31st in yards per play allowed (18.3) when targeted deep.

Lions coach Dan Campbell knows that the Packers’ two deep receivers, Christian Watson and Matthew Golden, could be a problem on Sunday when the two teams face off.

“It presents some big challenges because these aren’t guys that can just track the ball down. They have got speed now. I mean, they have got speed and they can track the ball and the quarterback gives them a nice pretty ball, man, lays it out there,” Campbell said. “And really about 50 percent of these are either DPI or catches, which is talk about explosive. So, that’s the danger in it.”

But as Campbell was quick to point out, the Lions can’t afford to just play their safeties deep, hoping to eliminate deep shots, because that’s when Packers tight end Tucker Kraft takes over.

“If you’re going to use it to take the top off on some of this, well now you have got Kraft underneath and you have got to worry about the backs. It does, it creates some issues, man, that you have got to be ready for,” Campbell said.

So on this week’s Midweek Mailbag, Erik Schlitt and I discuss the options for defending the Packers’ passing attack. What role should Brian Branch play in defending the pass? Should he try to erase Kraft over the middle of the field? Is he best used this week at nickel, box safety, or deep safety—or a combination of all three? And is this the week to heavily rely on the athletic Keith Abney? Or should Detroit play it more safe with a veteran like Chuck Clark?

Other topics on this week’s show include:

  • What is the Lions’ biggest advantage over the Packers? And what is Green Bay’s biggest advantage over Detroit?
  • How much will Josh Jacobs’ return this week matter?
  • Will the Lions utilize more 21 personnel (two running back sets) or max protection against the Packers’ and Vikings’ aggressive defense?
  • Outside of the secondary, where do the Lions need to improve most to compete for a Super Bowl?
  • If the defense continues to improve, should the Lions still trade for a cornerback?
  • Given Detroit’s slow start, why should anyone be optimistic the Lions can turn it around this year?

Check out the entire show using the Spotify embed below or searching “Pride of Detroit” on your favorite podcasting platform.

You can catch a longer version of the Midweek Mailbag by heading over to our YouTube page or Twitch channel and watching this week’s show. In the longer version, we also gave our reactions to Sam LaPorta’s expressions of frustration over contract negotiations.

item.title: Another Rams starter lands on injury report
item.description: Nate Landman could miss Week 7, joining a long list of injured Rams
item.content:encoded:
Linebacker Nate Landman could miss Week 7 after he entered the concussion protocol on Wednesday. The Los Angeles Rams have already lost several key starters this week, including Davante Adams and Kobie Turner, but now their top linebacker could be held out against the Las Vegas Raiders.

What the Rams need is to be healthy, and that’s not happening. Will L.A. get healthy? Will Myles Garrett play again this season?

Things aren’t looking good. You know what would make things look better? If the Rams could find way to win on Sunday, but that looks less likely each day this week as the injuries continue to pile up.

The team can say they aren’t giving up, but at a certain point this season will be lost, unless they can turn it around. The way the Rams turn this all around is with a win. Now, they may have to find a way to win without Landman.

Rams LB Nate Landman in concussion protocol (ramswire)

“Only missing one play, Landman recorded 71 snaps on Sunday during the team’s loss to the Arizona Cardinals, picking up 10 total tackles. Since joining the Rams last season, he has not missed a game for the franchise. This season, he has 51 total tackles (27 solo), six stuffs, and two forced fumbles.

If he is unable to play, Omar Speights should be the player to step up in his role, while Shaun Dolac and Grant Stuard will serve as backups. Considering the team’s heavy use of their nickel and dime defense, Landman’s potential absence could lead to problems on the interior as they’re set to face the tight end duo of Brock Bowers and Michael Mayer this week when they play the Las Vegas Raiders.“

Rams Get Ominous Injury Timeline Update on Myles Garrett (sports.yahoo)

“Rams head coach Sean McVay announced in Week 6 that Garrett would not return to action.

McVay did the same ahead of Week 7. Unfortunately, it appears Rams fans could hear that familiar refrain for several more weeks.

This comes as at least a mild surprise after previous reports suggested it was possible that Garrett could return in Week 7. Garrett also received a possible six-to-eight-week timeline, which would put his return at Weeks 8 through 10.“

Rams waiting to schedule Adams’ (hammy) surgery (nbcsports)

“Surgeries are sometimes delayed to help reduce swelling. Occasionally, new information is gathered during this time and/or during the surgery. Adams is currently expected to be sidelined for 6-10 weeks. Perhaps the wide return-to-play timeline is due to the fact that the surgeon has not yet fully assessed the injury. We tentatively expect the team to share an updated recovery timeline once Adams undergoes the procedure on his ruptured hamstring tendon. Stay tuned.”

Rams have no consolation prize waiting in 2027 draft (no matter how the season ends) (ramblinfan)

“Los Angeles made 14 draft selections in 2023. Shockingly, nine of those players are still with the team, and many are vital starters. That’s how the Rams were able to rebound so quickly. Rather than cling to veterans, they shed highly compensated stars, gathered as many draft picks as possible, and completely overhauled the roster.

What felt like insanity at the time proved to be inspired wisdom. On a roster filled with holes, rookies easily earned starting roles. The team benefited from developing plug-and-play dynamos who have become the roster’s core.

The gamble paid off with a jackpot. With a first-round draft pick, the Rams had to begin the rebuild in Round 2. They made the practical decision to commit their first three selections to addressing the line of scrimmage on both sides of the ball.“

Rams face another looming threat as Puka Nacua’s NFL review drags on (nypost)

“Wide receiver Puka Nacua and left tackle Alaric Jackson remain under league review for off-field incidents, NFL spokesman Brian McCarthy told The California Post on Wednesday. There is no timeline for a decision in either matter.

That leaves the Rams trying to rescue their season while waiting to learn whether their path will become even more difficult.

The hope had been to build enough of a cushion in the standings to absorb potential suspensions. Instead, the Rams have left themselves little margin for error, and an injury to wide receiver Davante Adams has further complicated their situation.“

CELEBRITY PHOTOS: Blue Man Group, Travis Bennett, Jordan McCullough & more celebrities in attendance at SoFi Stadium for the Rams’ Week 6 matchup vs. the Cardinals (therams)

“The stars were out at SoFi Stadium on Sunday! Swipe through photos of Blue Man Group, Travis Bennett, Jordan McCullough & more celebs in attendance as the Los Angeles Rams took on the Arizona Cardinals in Week 6.”

Matthew Stafford and Puka Nacua discuss Rams’ loss to Cardinals in postgame press conference (nfl.com)

“Los Angeles Rams quarterback Matthew Stafford and wide receiver Puka Nacua discuss the Rams’ loss to the Arizona Cardinals in the postgame press conference”

Rams drop in Week 7 power rankings (therams)

“Here is the power ranking roundup heading into Week 7.

USA Today: 13

As they enter a new Bill Parcells reality − “You are what your record says you are” − the Rams (2-4) have also added injuries to Sunday’s (latest) insult. Moving forward, they won’t have WR Davante Adams (hamstring) or DL Kobie Turner for at least the next month. NT Poona Ford is out for the year. And the kicker? Sean McVay needs another one of those, too.“

The Rams and Chargers are both a mess, and it’s only getting worse (sports.yahoo)

“The preseason hype surrounding football in Los Angeles was real. The Rams made bold, splashy moves to tweak an already stellar team and presumably turn them into a monster. The Chargers retooled their coaching staff, adding vaunted offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel in a move assumed would finally get the hapless franchise over the hump and into contention.

Fast-forward six weeks and both organizations are a dumpster fire. The Rams (2-4) have drastically underperformed their potential, losing to the Cardinals over the weekend and finding themselves at the bottom of the NFC West with no clear way to catch up. The Chargers (0-6) are even worse, boasting one of the worst offenses in the NFL, hurtling towards a No. 1 overall pick, with a coaching staff that seems incapable of turning the ship around.

The idea of an all-Los Angeles, Chargers vs. Rams Super Bowl at SoFi Stadium didn’t feel like it was outside the realm of possibility at one point. Now the notion of putting these teams together on football’s brightest stage is a hilarious joke. Neither team is likely to make the playoffs at all, and everything that could go wrong, has.“

Comment of the day:

“We’re going with a guy who used to be good but hasn’t been recently. Sounds like a good plan. I am losing my trust in this organizations ability to make good decisions. I am very interested to see what happens against the Raiders.

If we split with the Sea Hawks, lose to the Niners and Chiefs, and win every other remaining game, we would be 10-7 which may not be good enough with tie breakers. That’s our margin for error to be a wild card. It is possible but highly unlikely considering the way we are playing. It’s very possible for us to win the next 4 and then things get much more difficult. However, this week is probably the toughest of the next 4. It will be interesting to see what we’re made of. After losing to the Cardinals, it’s tough to feel like we’ve just been unlucky since it wasn’t a fluke and they flat out played us. It was really a must win and we didn’t show up. Hopefully we’ll get it together this week.“-JWgorams

item.title: Cowboys Week 7 opponent: A look at the 2026 Philadelphia Eagles
item.description: How nervous are you about the Eagles?
item.content:encoded:
The Dallas Cowboys are heading to Philadelphia for a Monday night NFC East showdown, and both teams have plenty of questions to answer. Dallas is coming off a 23-13 loss to Green Bay that dropped them to 2-4, while the Eagles have lost four straight and are also sitting at 2-4.

Philadelphia’s season has taken an especially dramatic turn, with quarterback Jalen Hurts sidelined for the year by blood clots and Tanner McKee stepping into the starting role.

The Eagles still have recognizable talent on both sides of the ball, including running back Saquon Barkley and wide receiver DeVonta Smith. But their offense has struggled to find a rhythm, and losing Hurts only makes that challenge more complicated.

Their defense has been the steadier unit, giving Philadelphia a chance to stay competitive even when the offense cannot sustain drives.

For Dallas, the opportunity is obvious: take advantage of an offense in transition. The challenge is that divisional games rarely follow the script, especially when the opposing defense can make life difficult.

Tanner McKee takes over as the Eagles’ quarterback

The biggest story in Philadelphia is the absence of Hurts. The Eagles confirmed that he will miss the remainder of the 2026 season after further testing revealed blood clots in his lungs. The focus is rightly on his recovery, but the football implications are enormous for a team that has struggled even with its starting quarterback available.

Hurts had thrown for 933 yards, eight touchdowns and three interceptions in five games before being sidelined. Replacing his production and leadership is a big ask, especially for a backup quarterback who hadn’t played a snap in the 2026 regular season before taking over against Carolina.

McKee made his first start of the season in Week 6, completing 26 of 45 passes for 215 yards and one touchdown without an interception in a 25-14 loss to the Panthers. The stat line was respectable in terms of ball security, but the offense managed only 222 net yards and struggled to generate consistent momentum.

McKee has shown flashes during his limited NFL opportunities, and he deserves time to settle into the role. Still, the Eagles cannot expect him to replicate everything Hurts brings to the offense. He is a different type of quarterback, and Philadelphia will likely need to simplify its approach, protect him better and create more manageable down-and-distance situations.

Dallas has struggled to generate consistent pressure this season, so getting after McKee without allowing easy underneath completions should be a priority. The Cowboys cannot afford to let an offense in transition find its confidence early.

Saquon Barkley and DeVonta Smith remain the key weapons

Even with the quarterback change, Philadelphia has playmakers capable of causing problems. Barkley remains the centerpiece of the running game when healthy, while Smith gives McKee a reliable target who can win at multiple levels of the field.

The major caveat is Barkley’s health. He missed Philadelphia’s last two games with a hamstring injury, and the Eagles have had to patch together their backfield in his absence. Through the first six weeks, Barkley had recorded 36 carries for 182 yards, averaging 5.1 yards per attempt, but he had not scored a rushing touchdown. Those numbers are limited by his missed time, and his availability for the Cowboys game will be an important storyline to watch as the week progresses.

Without Barkley, Philadelphia has struggled to establish a consistent ground attack. The Eagles used Dameon Pierce and Carson Steele against Carolina after injuries depleted the depth chart, and the team finished with only 62 rushing yards. That lack of production puts even more pressure on McKee and the passing game.

Smith offers a more established option in the passing game. He returned from a hamstring injury against Carolina and caught a touchdown pass from McKee. Through six games, Smith has 26 receptions for 310 yards and two touchdowns. He gives the Eagles a receiver who can separate, make contested catches and create opportunities when the offense needs a spark.

The question is whether Philadelphia can build a functional offense around those pieces. Smith’s return is a positive, and if Barkley is available, Dallas will have to account for his ability to turn a small crease into a substantial gain. If he remains sidelined, the Cowboys should be able to focus more attention on the passing game.

Philadelphia’s defense is keeping it competitive

The Eagles’ defense has been the more dependable side of the team, and it could be the biggest obstacle for Dallas on Monday night. Philadelphia has not been perfect, but it has created more disruption than its offense has generated, recording eight sacks and three interceptions through six games.

The defense also has young playmakers capable of changing a possession. Defensive tackle Jalen Carter and edge rusher Nolan Smith have each recorded three sacks, while cornerbacks Cooper DeJean and Quinyon Mitchell have each intercepted a pass. Linebacker Jihaad Campbell has contributed across the defense, giving Philadelphia another young player to build around.

The unit’s job has become more difficult because the offense has struggled to sustain drives. Philadelphia’s defense played 79 snaps against Carolina, compared with 64 for the Eagles’ offense. That imbalance can wear down even a talented group, particularly when the offense repeatedly gives the ball back without putting points on the board.

Still, the defense has done enough to keep the Eagles within reach in several games. Yet against Carolina, the Eagles allowed 25 points and struggled to stop the run, showing the defense isn’t immune to the same inconsistency affecting the rest of the roster.

For Dallas, the matchup presents a familiar challenge. The Cowboys’ offense has shown it can move the ball, but the loss to Green Bay exposed problems with protection, rushing production and execution in critical moments. Philadelphia has enough talent up front and in the secondary to make those issues costly.

The Cowboys need to establish the run, keep Prescott out of obvious passing situations and avoid turnovers. If the offense becomes predictable, the Eagles have the personnel to pressure Prescott and force difficult throws. Dallas cannot assume that a struggling Philadelphia team will simply roll over, especially with a defense capable of creating momentum-changing plays.

A struggling offense, but no easy divisional game

Philadelphia enters Week 7 on a four-game losing streak, averaging just 14.5 points per game during that stretch. The Eagles have scored 14 points against Carolina, 17 against Jacksonville, 7 against Chicago and 20 against the Rams. The results point to a broader problem, which is their offense has not been very good.

Dallas has its own issues, of course. The Cowboys have lost consecutive games and are still searching for consistency on both sides of the ball. That makes Monday night an important test for a team that cannot afford to give a divisional opponent easy opportunities.

The recent history between these teams reinforces how little the records matter once they meet. Philadelphia beat Dallas 24-20 in the 2025 season opener, but the Cowboys responded with a 24-21 win in Philadelphia later that year. Dallas leads the all-time series, 75-59, but recent meetings have been competitive enough that neither team can take the other lightly. If the Cowboys allow the Eagles’ defense to dictate the pace, another frustrating night could be waiting in Philadelphia.

item.title: Week 7 NFL picks against the spread, predictions for every game: Chiefs look to stay undefeated vs. Seattle
item.description: The Seahawks are off to a bit of a disappointing start at 3-3.
item.content:encoded:
If the Kansas City Chiefs win on Sunday night, it will be a sign to the NFL that they plan to reclaim their spot in the Super Bowl.

The Chiefs had a rough 2025 season but that was clearly an aberration. They're 5-0 going into a primetime game against the Seattle Seahawks.

Kenneth Walker III is a key figure in both teams' stories this season.

Walker changed teams this offseason when the Seahawks let him go in free agency, and he signed with the Chiefs. Walker has reshaped the Chiefs' offense, with a league-high 665 rushing yards. While Walker has been tremendous in Kansas City, the Seahawks have struggled to find any consistency at running back without him. It's hurting their offense, because Sam Darnold is turning the ball over at a high rate with no running game to take pressure off him. The Seahawks are a disappointing 3-3 after winning the Super Bowl last season.

Seattle is still a quality opponent with a good home-field advantage. The defense is near the level it reached last season, when it was dominant. The offense is having its issues, but it's still capable. It wouldn't surprise anyone if Seattle rallied this season after a middling start and made it back to the Super Bowl.

That's what makes Sunday night an interesting game for the Chiefs. They do have solid wins and nothing about their start seems fraudulent. It's a good team. But a win at Seattle would stamp the Chiefs as a potentially great team this season.

On the other side, another loss would put the Seahawks under .500 with a three-game losing streak going into November. There will be urgency on their side, as well as the comfort of being back home. And it's not like the Seahawks are suddenly a bad team, even with a mediocre record. That's why Seattle -2.5 is the pick. It would be a very impressive win if the Chiefs can pull it off.

Here are the rest of the picks against the spread for Week 7 of the NFL season:

Patriots (+3) over Bears

This is a fun primetime matchup. It might not have been a few weeks ago, when Drake Maye was slumping and Caleb Williams was hurt, but Maye has heated up, Williams is healthy and both teams look pretty good at 4-2. There are injury concerns on both sides, but one that stands out is Bears running back Kyle Monangai. The Bears' rushing attack isn't quite the same without him sharing time with D'Andre Swift. These teams are evenly matched, so taking a field goal seems wise.

Saints (+3.5) over Steelers

The NFL goes to Paris, where the civil unrest in France has been a big part of the story surrounding the game. The Steelers have been the better team this season, as reflected by their 4-2 record. The 2-4 Saints did play well for three quarters against the Giants last week before letting down in the fourth quarter and letting the Giants back in the game. Despite the Steelers' record, it's hard to feel too confident in them.

Giants (+10.5) over Texans

You won't see a team above .500 as a double-digit underdog against a 2-4 team very often. Everyone understands it for this game: The Texans are better than their record and showed it in last week's win over the Jaguars, and the Giants are just getting by in their wins (and ties, in the case of the Commanders' late-game fiasco). The Giants are also onto their third quarterback of the season, replacing Jameis Winston with J.J. McCarthy after McCarthy's blazing hot fourth quarter last week. But perhaps McCarthy's late-game rally from last week carries over? Also, Houston is coming right off a game in London, and that isn't always ideal. Houston is laying a lot of points.

Falcons (+3) over 49ers

This line looks a little strange, doesn't it? The 49ers are the best team in the NFL so far. The Falcons are 2-4 and coming off a game in which they trailed 31-7 in the fourth quarter to the Bears at home. The 49ers' injuries, particularly one to Mike Evans, has to factor in. Evans left Monday night's game with an Achilles injury and the 49ers offense struggled without him. They are decimated at receiver. Evans could play, but it's hard to assume he'll be fully healthy. Laying only three points with the 49ers feels like a trap.

Panthers (-3) over Buccaneers

Baker Mayfield seems likely to be back this week. And the Buccaneers are desperate for a big win to get back in the NFC South race. It might not matter. The Bucs are still a poorly coached team while the Panthers aren't getting the respect they've earned yet.

Browns (-1.5) over Titans

The Titans got their first win, and perhaps that's a sign that they're improving. Let's wait to see it again though. One half doesn't completely erase that Tennessee was the second-worst team in the NFL for their first five-and-a-half games.

Bengals (-1.5) over Ravens

It's an impossible game to pick at this point in the week because we don't know if Lamar Jackson, who was limited in practice on Wednesday with an ankle injury, will play. Everything changes if he's back. For now we'll guess and say he will sit out, and that won't be good news against a Bengals team coming off a bye.

Jets (-4.5) over Dolphins

The Dolphins aren't going to have many games in which they have a realistic chance to win. This is one of them. The 2-4 Jets aren't very good. But let's also be honest: They're far better than this Dolphins team.

Vikings (-6.5) over Colts

The Colts lost to the Titans, fired general manager Chris Ballard afterward and coach Shane Steichen could be next. We know that in this NFL season, nothing seems predictable. But it's too hard to pick a Colts team in chaos against an undefeated Vikings team.

Cardinals (+4.5) over Broncos

Until the Broncos' offense improves, it's too hard to pick them laying points on the road. It's not like the Cardinals are incapable; they just beat the Rams on the road. And Denver, which had 38 yards after halftime last week against Seattle, has been poor on offense all season.

Packers (+3) over Lions

The Packers have looked good two weeks in a row, though those games came against bad defenses. Well, here's another bad defense for them. We all know the script for Lions games by now: Detroit's defense will give up a ton of points and the offense's job is to win a shootout. That could happen against a Packers defense that is hard to figure out after a bad start to the season and then two good games. Either way, taking the points against a bad defense is often the right call.

Raiders (+4.5) over Rams

At some point the Rams could break out. But for now, the Rams are a mediocre team that is now taking on injuries, including a key one to Davante Adams. And the Raiders' three-game losing streak might fool you. They led the Chiefs in the fourth quarter, were blown out by the Patriots in a tough spot and then were tied with the Bills in the fourth quarter. Las Vegas might not be a playoff team this season, but it's far better than in years past.

Eagles (+4.5) over Cowboys

Well, this isn't the NFC East Monday night showdown the NFL was hoping for when the schedule was released. The Eagles are bad and now without Jalen Hurts, and the Cowboys are bad too. If anything is going to bring out an inspired performance from the Eagles, it's a primetime matchup against their rival. And it's not like Dallas' defense can stop anyone.

item.title: NFL Week 7 Survivor/Eliminator Picks
item.description: This is the weirdest time of year in NFL Survivor contests. If you’re still chugging along in yours, you’ve likely run through some of the most obvious teams. Later in the season, it’s not about picking from a wealth of…
item.content:encoded:
This is the weirdest time of year in NFL Survivor contests. If you’re still chugging along in yours, you’ve likely run through some of the most obvious teams. Later in the season, it’s not about picking from a wealth of decent choices; it’s about picking what’s still available. But right now? Week 7? You still have some options. Maybe not all the options, maybe not the elite teams, but you have options. It’s not picking from the A-plusses, but it’s not taking whatever C-minus falls to you. Everything is a B, B-plus, and you have to pick among them. That’s hard. Let’s see how that plays out. Check out my Week 7 pick for Survivor contests. And while we’re here, you can use our NFL Betting Model and our Bet Tracker to make a pick for yourself.

NFL Survivor Picks for Week 7

Every week, we have the same process. We eliminate teams in groups until we narrow it down to our real considerations. Start with all 32, whittle it down. And remember — this game is “once you use a team, they’re off the board,” so it’s not always just a matter of taking the team you think will win. There has to be some strategy. I can’t pick a team I’ve picked before, but you might not have tailed me, so previously used teams are eligible until the end.

Bye Weeks

My favorite category — picks I can’t get wrong! If you don’t play, you can’t win, but also I won’t pick you, so woohoo for easy. Buffalo Bills Jacksonville Jaguars Los Angeles Chargers Washington Commanders That’s four off the board.

Opponent Is Too Good

Maybe these are good teams, maybe not, but it’s too hard to trust them given who they are facing. This is a 10-team list every week (fewer when there are byes); we are eliminating anyone facing a top-10 team in our FTN NFL Power Rankings. Arizona Cardinals (vs. Denver) Atlanta Falcons (vs. San Francisco) Chicago Bears (vs. New England) Cincinnati Bengals (@ Baltimore) Indianapolis Colts (@ Minnesota) Kansas City Chiefs (@ Seattle) New England Patriots (@ Chicago) Seattle Seahawks (vs. Kansas City) Some of these teams will win but you can’t confidently say so, considering who they’re facing. That’s eight more gone, 20 to go.

They’re Too Bad

You can face the worst team in all of football, but if you’re the second-worst team, well, I’m still not going to be too excited about selecting you. We’ll return to the power rankings here and cross off any team in the bottom 12. Miami Dolphins (@ NY Jets) New Orleans Saints (vs. Pittsburgh in France) New York Giants (@ Houston) New York Jets (vs. Miami) Philadelphia Eagles (vs. Dallas) Tampa Bay Buccaneers (@ Carolina) Tennessee Titans (vs. Cleveland) Seven more eliminations leaves us with 13 remaining.

Island Games

Island games just get weird. I would need some very convincing evidence to pick anyone on a Thursday, or a Monday, or an overseas 9:30 a.m. ET game. There aren’t many left this week, but I still want to note them. Dallas Cowboys (@ Philadelphia) Pittsburgh Steelers (vs. New Orleans in France) Two more gone, 11 left. But this week, we have one extra category.

Who’s Playing for Them?

There is a startling number of teams in turmoil right now. These are teams that would normally still be eligible through this point in our process, but I can eliminate them in one fell swoop with a simple question: Can we trust that their lineup this week is who we want it to be? Baltimore Ravens (vs. Cincinnati) — Lamar Jackson back? And is he 100% if so? Denver Broncos (@ Arizona) — The number of “will Bo Nix get benched?” questions is only rising. Los Angeles Rams (@ Las Vegas) — So many injuries last week. It’s a mess. San Francisco 49ers (@ Atlanta) — Eventually a team loses too many receivers. And that’s four more gone, leaving us with seven teams — our seven contenders.

The Contenders

Once we’re down to this small a number of teams, we’re done cutting them in swaths. We look at the pros and cons for each team and then figure it out. I’m also diving into our NFL Betting Model to see what the numbers think of the game.

Carolina Panthers (vs. Tampa Bay)

Model Projection: Lions 25.06-23.81, Packers 46.8% win rate Pros: With Josh Jacobs expected to be back, the Packers are all set up to have the offense they planned to have. Cons: Would you feel comfortable resting your whole season on either side of this rivalry game?

Model Projection: Texans 27.92-16.58, Texans 78.6% win rate Pros: The Texans are suddenly 2-4 and C.J. Stroud looks like a star again. Cons: It was two weeks ago that everyone was giving up on Houston. Meanwhile, the Giants are actually in first place.

Model Projection: Rams 29.41-20.29, Raiders 28.3% win rate Pros: The Rams are falling apart. Cons: Even a falling-apart Rams team is pretty talented. Meanwhile, the Raiders have fallen from 3-0 to 3-3.

Model Projection: Vikings 25.65-17.17, Vikings 73.2% win rate Pros: The best defense in football attacking whatever it is that Daniel Jones is now? Goodness. Cons: The Vikings offense still doesn’t scare anyone.

The Texans have righted the ship, while the Giants are a mess and are J.J. McCarthy out there. I trust Houston to keep it rolling this week.
